source_evidence.observation: The paper defines F = {m·β^e : m,e ∈ Z, -β^p < m < β^p, e_min ≤ e ≤ e_max}, where β is the base and p is the mantissa length.

A computed operation satisfies x ⊙ y = fl(x·y), and similarly for addition and subtraction; unless stated otherwise, fl rounds to a nearest member of F. FastTwoSum computes s ← x ⊕ y, t ← s ⊖ x, and e ← y ⊖ t.
The exact-transform conclusion denoted by equation (3) is s + e = x + y with s = x ⊕ y; the unadorned operations in this identity are real operations.
For r in (-β^(e_max+p), β^(e_max+p)), ulp(r) is min{g-f : f,g ∈ F ∪ {β^(e_max+p)}, f ≤ |r| < g}.

For FastTwoSum inputs x,y ∈ F, nearest addition and faithful subtraction suffice for equation (3) if some representation of x satisfies |y| ≤ floor(β^p-β/2)·β^e(x). The theorem does not restrict β to {2,3}.

Throughout Section 4, operations are rounded to nearest unless otherwise specified, overflow is generally assumed absent, and any base restrictions or underflow exceptions are to be stated in the individual application.

FourSumThreeProduct calls TwoProduct successively on (x2,x3), (x1,t_h), and (x1,t_l), producing (t_h,t_l), (s1,s2'), and (s3',s4'). TwoProduct transforms a product into two floating-point addends and is error-free if neither underflow nor overflow occurs.
The first TwoProduct call satisfies t_h+t_l=x2·x3, t_h=x2⊙x3, and |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x2·x3). Applying the corresponding contracts to the next two calls gives s1+Σ(i=2 to 4)s_i'=Π(i=1 to 3)x_i.
ThreeProduct first obtains (s1,s2',s3',s4') from FourSumThreeProduct, then computes (s2,s3'') ← FastTwoSum(s2',s3'), and finally computes s3 ← s3'' ⊕ s4'.
Lemma 4 assumes the absence of underflow errors within the FourSumThreeProduct call and concludes Σ(i=1 to 3)s_i=Π(i=1 to 3)x_i.
After treating x1x2x3=0 as trivial, the proof invokes invariance under power-of-β scaling, subject to no overflow or underflow, and normalizes ulp(x_i)=1. It then has x_i ∈ Z and max_i |x_i|≤β^p-1.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 4 proof, FastTwoSum merge and final addition
source_evidence.observation: The proof establishes condition (7) for the pair (s2',s3'), hence s2+s3''=s2'+s3'. It then proves |s3''|≤β^p/2 and |s4'|≤β^p/2, so s3''+s4' is an integer in F and the final rounded addition is exact.

contract_plain_english: Fix the paper's floating-point system and nearest-rounded Section 4 operations, with overflow absent. For any three floating-point inputs x1,x2,x3, FourSumThreeProduct first decomposes x2x3, then decomposes x1 times each of that decomposition's two terms into an exact four-term expansion. [PDF pp. 9 and 13-14, printed pp. 391 and 395-396, anchors: Section 4 assumptions, FourSumThreeProduct, and equation (17)] Assuming no underflow errors in those delegated product transformations, ThreeProduct applies the original FastTwoSum to the two middle terms. The proof establishes the representation-dependent condition (7), without requiring a base restriction or magnitude/ULP ordering, so this merge is exact. It then proves that the FastTwoSum residual and the fourth product term have an exactly representable sum, making the final rounded addition exact. [PDF pp. 14-15, printed pp. 396-397, anchors: ThreeProduct, condition-(7) argument, and final-add argument] Consequently, the three computed outputs satisfy s1+s2+s3=x1x2x3 exactly, with no omitted or higher-order error term. [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4, equation (18)]
